steps.label: Use the aᵘ rule with base 7
steps.margin_note: First mark. The base 7 is fixed and the power varies, so this is aᵘ, not uⁿ. The logₑ7 factor belongs to the aᵘ rule and must appear on this line.
steps.memory_tip: Constant base with a varying power brings down the logarithm of the base. Varying base with a constant power does not.

recall.must_convey: That the rule d/dx(aᵘ) = aᵘ · logₑa · du/dx is used with a = 7 and u = x³ + 3x.

steps.why: Choosing the rule is the whole decision in this question. The power rule d/dx(uⁿ) = nuⁿ⁻¹ applies when the power is a fixed number; here the power moves with x and the base does not, so the exponential rule applies instead. logₑ7 means the natural logarithm of 7, written simply as log 7 at this level.
common_mistakes: Using the power rule and writing (x³ + 3x)·7ˣ³⁺³ˣ⁻¹.

steps.label: Differentiate the exponent and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The exponent differentiates term by term to 3x² + 3. Taking 3 out as 3(x² + 1) is the tidy form an examiner expects.
steps.memory_tip: The exponent x³ + 3x gives 3x² + 3, and both terms carry a 3, so 3(x² + 1) comes out in one move.

recall.must_convey: That the exponent differentiates to 3x² + 3 = 3(x² + 1), giving 3(x² + 1)·7ˣ³⁺³ˣ·logₑ7.
